scope: Configuration-driven four Z calibration using native step generation, simulated MCU serial links and a real HTTP product service. Compiled package and physical hardware acceptance are pending.
checks: Exactly four configured independent Z motors and two opposite gantry corners
Ordered nondegenerate probe rows, axis ranges, probe offsets and retry policy validated before startup
Conflicting Z tilt, bed tilt or CoreXZ rejected
Shared automatic probe ownership with independent four-rail geometric solver
Flat, single pass, convergence, exhausted retries, increasing range and invalid travel
Authenticated HTTP calibration, unhomed rejection, coordinate synchronization and applied status
Completed request replay returns the same result with no new motor packets
Existing product startup, shutdown, pressure tuning, object queries and endpoint exclusivity regressions

performance.scope: Test duration includes startup, four-point probing, calibration and teardown, and ran alongside calibration regression. Not an isolated latency or print throughput benchmark. Numerical and segmented execution code did not change in this integration.

limitations: The default Python printing entrypoint remains; no Python files retired.
The 120 second API deadline bounds all retries together.
Applied does not prove a post-adjustment measurement meets tolerance.
Maximum travel is per pass and quantization occurs at each segment.
